 Democrats push minimum-wage hikes after midterm gains as economists warn of risks
 Saturday, 14 November 2026, 12:16 
 Photo source: Fox News 
 The proposals are drawing scrutiny over their possible effects on small businesses and inexperienced workers, concerns also raised in debate over Seattle’s higher minimum wage. 
 After Democrats’ 2026 midterm victories, Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro is proposing to raise his state’s minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour - an increase of roughly 107%. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, who signed a 2019 law gradually raising Illinois’ minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2025, is urging Congress to increase the federal minimum wage. Affordability is a central part of Democrats’ governing agenda.
 This is reported by Fox News .
 Tom Savidge, an economist with the American Institute for Economic Research, told Fox News Digital that sharp increases could lead small businesses to raise prices, cut workers’ hours or hire fewer people. “A federal minimum wage hike will worsen the affordability crisis,” Savidge said. He warned that a single national mandate would ignore regional differences in wages and business costs, and could mean fewer hours and jobs, particularly for inexperienced workers. He also said large corporations may be better able than small businesses to absorb higher labor costs by spreading them across more sales, investing in automation or relocating operations.
 Advertisement 
 Seattle, where the minimum wage is currently $21.30 an hour and is set to rise to $22.14 in January, is one example cited in the debate. In December 2025, KOMO News reported that some local business owners had raised concerns about added costs. Fox News Digital previously reported that Seattle restaurant owners who closed locations cited rising labor costs alongside higher food prices, declining customer demand and other operating expenses. A January survey by The Intentionalist found that 67% of 136 independent small businesses in Seattle and surrounding Washington communities reported more financial strain than during the pandemic. Respondents cited rising labor costs, rent and insurance, as well as weaker customer demand.
 Research on Seattle’s wage increases has produced different findings. A 2022 study in the American Economic Journal: Economic Policy found that the city’s 2015 and 2016 increases boosted pay for longer-tenured workers but reduced hours worked, particularly for less-experienced employees, and limited opportunities for people entering low-wage jobs. A separate 2017 study by University of California, Berkeley researchers found that earlier increases raised food-service wages without a statistically significant decline in restaurant employment.
 Shapiro has made the increase a priority after Democrats won control of both chambers of Pennsylvania’s legislature. Democrats secured a trifecta in Harrisburg in the 2026 midterms after flipping the state Senate. Shapiro said half a million workers in Pennsylvania still earn less than $15 an hour and pledged that the first bill he signs with the new Democratic majority in January will raise the minimum wage. His office referred Fox News Digital to comments he made about the proposal in an interview with former CNN host Don Lemon released on Sunday.
 The push is also gaining support in Congress. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Monday that the federal minimum wage should be raised and that he plans to discuss the issue with members of both chambers. Jeffries said it had not been increased in 20 years and is currently $7.25 per hour.
 Adam Gorcyca, a policy researcher at the Illinois Policy Institute, said employers may respond to higher labor costs by cutting hours, slowing hiring or raising prices, potentially making it harder for entry-level and younger workers to find jobs. He also questioned whether Illinois’ increases had delivered broader employment gains, saying the state was among the slowest to recover from the pandemic. Pritzker’s office did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on Tuesday.
